title: Cycles of discourse, speech dysfluency, and active inference.
title_zh: 话语周期、语言不流畅与主动推断
abstract: Speech is a complex motor and social act. We must not only produce and understand sequences of variable-length words formed from ordered syllables but also speak and listen in turn. This theoretical article introduces a computational model of speech production and auditory segmentation based on sequences of discrete phonemes. The purpose of this model is to develop a vehicle for testing (in silico) hypotheses about the mechanisms that govern the loss of speech fluency, something may occur transiently in people who stutter or progressively in various neurodegenerative conditions. The modeling presented here employs Partially Observable Markov Decision Processes that provide a useful generic formulation for specifying the internal model that our brains might use to describe dynamic environments in which they can exert partial control and make partial observations. The core features of the specific model used here are as follows: (a) a reciprocal mapping from words to sequences of varying numbers of phonemes and (b) a common subset of states for both speech generation and speech perception. A further novel feature is a social component in which one must infer who is speaking (oneself or another person). We propose a series of hypotheses about the computational mechanisms that might underwrite speech breakdown. For example, we demonstrate that reducing the precision in the next word introduces pauses and start-of-word repetitions of the sort associated with stuttering. We examine the patterns of behavior and belief-updating predicted by each of these hypotheses, with implications for both speaking and listening. Finally, we discuss plausible neural substrates for the underlying message passing that might be amenable to interrogation with functional imaging. abstract_zh: 说话是一项复杂的运动和社会行为。我们不仅要产生和理解由有序音节组成的可变长度单词序列，还要进行轮流说话和倾听。本理论文章介绍了一种基于离散音素序列的语音产生和听觉分割计算模型。该模型旨在为体内（in silico）测试关于控制语言流畅性丧失机制的假设提供一个载体，这种丧失在口吃者中可能是暂时的，也可能在各种神经退行性疾病中逐渐发生。此处提出的模型采用部分可观测马尔可夫决策过程，为指定我们大脑可能用来描述动态环境（其中大脑可以部分控制并作部分观察）的内部模型提供了有用的通用公式。这里使用的具体模型的核心特征如下：(a) 单词与不同数量的音素序列之间的双向映射，以及(b) 语音产生和语音感知之间共同的状态子集。另一个新特征是社会组成部分，其中必须推断谁在说话（自己还是另一个人）。我们提出了一系列关于可能支撑语言中断的计算机制的假设。例如，我们展示了降低下一个单词的精度会引入与口吃相关的停顿和单词开头重复。我们考察了每个假设预测的行为和信念更新模式，对说话和倾听均有影响。最后，我们讨论了潜在的神经底物，这些底物可能支撑底层消息传递，并可能通过功能影像学进行探究。（PsycInfo 数据库记录（c）2026 APA，保留所有权利。）
